====Vox Collar====
{{Transcript|text=
I almost wrote off [[Monongah|Monongah Township]] as a whole, but that one house on the outskirts of town proved fruitful in my search for old [[Technology|tech]].

A scientist named [[Eddie Harrison|Dr. Harrison]] built a functioning interpreter for animal sounds. With a little bit of tinkering, I was able to improve upon his work. 

It should allow a [[human]] or animal, incapable of speech, to produce words we can understand. For now, it is limited to the voice library that Dr. Harrison provided, but if it works, I can always add more.
}}

====Water Purifier====
{{Transcript|text=
Found a solution to the [[water]] problem. [[Toxic water]] is what you get for settling in a place the locals called the [[Toxic Valley]]. But [[Meg Groberg|Meg]] just had to insist on using this old space station as a base.

Luckily, I scrapped some of the station's water filtration systems and was able to rig it up to our [[Water purifier (Fallout 76)|purifiers]] to make just about anything drinkable. We still have to clean out the excess sludge buildup almost daily, but as long as we do that, we've got clean water.
}}

====Tracking Beacon====
{{Small|'''Note:''' ''Accessing this entry advances the optional path in the [[Fallout 76 quests|quest]] [[Cheating Death]], allowing the player character to confront Fisher over what he knows about Lou.''}}
{{Transcript|text=
The latest salvage from the station yielded some fancy radio equipment I haven't seen before. What's unique about this is how small they managed to make it. I suppose that size is a concern when bringing equipment to space.

I constructed a basic tracking device and built it into the collar. It seems [[Weasel]] was able to follow [[Lucky Lou|Lou]]'s trail, and by using a [[Fisher's tracking beacon|simple radio]], I can tune in and track down Weasel's, and therefore, Lou's location by following the tones from the tracking device.

If Meg finds out I let him go, or that I know where he is, she'll have my head. Best to find an opportunity to slip away and get them back before anyone notices they were gone.
}}

====Space Beam====
{{Transcript|text=
I'm not sure what sort of work they were doing up on the space station, but I dug into some of the surviving documents. 

This thing they were building. It's not like anything I've seen before. Is it communications? A weapon? I don't know. There's a lot of missing information.

I've decided to call it the "Space Beam," for lack of better words. [[Munch]] wanted to call it the "Angel Piss Project," of course,  but I quickly put an end to that.

It could be years before I figure it all out, let alone get it running.
}}
====Power Armor====
{{Transcript|text=
Meg told me that she and the [[Raiders (Fallout 76)|other gangs]] used to tussle with these guys called the [[Brotherhood of Steel]], who'd roam around wearing [[power armor]], trying to restore order or something.

I told her I wanted a suit to tinker with, and she obliged, taking me to one of their old bases. We found one, barely functioning.

It's almost ready now. Just a few more tweaks and I think it'll be better than it ever was to begin with.
}}

====The Arena====
{{Transcript|text=

=====Entry 1=====
{{Transcript|text=
<nowiki>~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~</nowiki>
Place: The Arena
Location: Cranberry Bog, Watoga
Take: Caps, Chems, Revenge
<nowiki>~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~</nowiki>
Meg may have lost interest in the Arena, but now that I know [[Hal Gleeson|Hal]]'s there, I can't drop it. I got a plan to get inside, but it's a two person job, and something tells me Meg isn't going to let me use any of her people for what's she'd call a "personal affair."
}}

=====Entry 2=====
{{Small|'''Note''': ''The following entry only shows up after the completion of [[Fun and Games]].''}}
{{Transcript|text=
<nowiki>~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~</nowiki>
Place: The Arena
Location: Cranberry Bog, Watoga
Take: Caps, Chems, Revenge
<nowiki>~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~</nowiki>
Meg's taken an odd liking to a local [[Vault Dweller (Fallout 76)|Vault Dweller]]. Much to my surprise, this person's got grit. A real survivor. This Vault Dweller may be just who I need to get to Hal, and Meg wouldn't have a thing to say about it.
}}

=====Entry 3=====
{{Small|'''Note''': ''The following entry only shows up after the completion of [[The Ol' Weston Shuffle]], if the player character sticks to the plan.''}}
{{Transcript|text=
<nowiki>~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~</nowiki>
Place: The Arena
Location: Cranberry Bog, Watoga
Take: Caps, Chems
<nowiki>~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~</nowiki>
The job was a success thanks to our new Vault Dweller. After what I saw, Vault 79 should be a drop in the bucket. I'm going to leave this entry open since the Arena could still have future potential.
}}

=====Entry 3=====
{{Small|'''Note''': ''The following entry only shows up after the completion of The Ol' Weston Shuffle, if the player character abandons the plan and/or goes in shooting.''}}
{{Transcript|text=
<nowiki>~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~</nowiki>
Place: The Arena
Location: Cranberry Bog, Watoga
Take: Caps, Chems
<nowiki>~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~</nowiki>
The job was a mess, thanks to our new Vault Dweller. I've never seen such sloppy work. And Meg thinks we actually need this person? I'll let her know, but I got a feeling she'll never cut the Vault Dweller out at this point. Meg's too honorable for her own good. Once again, it's going to fall to me to clean up someone else's mess.

I'm going to leave this entry open since the Arena could still have future potential.
}}

====The Wayward====
{{Transcript|text=
<nowiki>~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~</nowiki>
Place: [[The Wayward]]
Location: [[The Forest]]
Take: Caps, Intel
<nowiki>~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~</nowiki>
I stopped by a recently opened bar called The Wayward. Lots of potential here. Travelers of all types. People constantly coming and going. I just need a persona to get in good with [[Duchess]] and I'm gold.
}}

====Foundation====
{{Transcript|text=
<nowiki>~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~</nowiki>
Place: [[Foundation]]
Location: Savage Divide
Take: Caps, Intel
<nowiki>~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~</nowiki>
Foundation is a target in more ways than one. Meg's going to be planning a lot of raids on those poor bastards. If I can get in good with them, I can charge for intel. Not only that, I can charge them for my own services if they feel like paying up.
}}

====Vault 79====
{{Transcript|text=
<nowiki>~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~</nowiki>
Place: [[Vault 79]]
Location: Savage Divide
Take: [[Gold bullion|Gold]]
<nowiki>~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~</nowiki>
I overheard Meg talking to the Vault Dweller about a whale of a heist. Apparently, good ole Uncle Sam hid all his gold in Vault 79 which just happens to be here right here in Appalachia.

Meg's got the Vault Dweller helping her put together a team, so this is the perfect opportunity to finally pull off that Arena job.
}}

===Personal Notes===
{{Transcript|text=
<nowiki>~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~</nowiki>
People of interest:
<nowiki>~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~</nowiki>
}}

====Hal (deceased)====
{{Small|'''Note''': ''The following entry only shows up after the completion of The Ol' Weston Shuffle.''}}
{{Transcript|text=
<nowiki>~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~</nowiki>
Person of Interest: Hal Gleeson
<nowiki>~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~</nowiki>
I screwed up. I'm a selfish asshole and Hal paid the price. I should've let him go or convinced him to stay.

He's the most solid partner I ever had. The only real relationship I ever had. Hell, probably the only real thing in general I ever had.

He's dead, and it's my fault. I'll never forgive myself.
}}

====The Vault Dweller====
{{Transcript|text=
<nowiki>~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~</nowiki>
Person of Interest: Vault Dweller
<nowiki>~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~</nowiki>
You wouldn't think someone living in a vault all this time would have any skills that mattered in a world like this. But this Dweller is one to watch, and Meg agrees. 

We'll all be running this heist Meg's got cooking for Vault 79. It should be an interesting test of skill for everyone involved. We'll see what this Vault Dweller's made of. Hope they've got some negotiating skills because I'll be testing those for damn sure.
}}

====Rose====
{{Transcript|text=
<nowiki>~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~</nowiki>
Person of Interest: [[Rose (Fallout 76)|Rose]] ([[Miss Nanny (Fallout 76)|Miss Nanny]])
<nowiki>~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~</nowiki>
I came across this crack pot of a Miss Nanny. Calls herself Rose and claims to be a "Raider." She's going on and on about the "Raider Ways" and trying to test out some old methods, as if I have time for that.

But she has knowledge of what happened here, so she could be a valuable asset. I figure, if anything, she also claims to have a cache that may have something of value hidden inside.
}}

====Duchess====
{{Transcript|text=
<nowiki>~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~</nowiki>
Person of Interest: Duchess
<nowiki>~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~</nowiki>
Duchess runs the Wayward, a fairly new establishment here in [[Appalachia]]. The woman's got moxie, and if I didn't know any better, I'd say she could even give Meg a run for her money.

She's got a business that's bringing in the caps and attracting people from all over. That means information I can sell, use, or both.
}}

====Paige====
{{Transcript|text=
<nowiki>~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~</nowiki>
Person of Interest: [[Paige]]
<nowiki>~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~</nowiki>
From what I can tell, Foundation is run by a guy named Paige. Very no-nonsense. Not really my type for business, but I can't pass on Foundation as a potential opportunity. He's smart though, not manipulated by the idea of caps or chems like most. I'll have to play my cards right if I want to pursue this one.
}}

==Location==

==Transcript==
[[File:A lead at last.ogg|center]]
{{Transcript|text=
'''[[Jack Hunter]]''': {{tooltip|[[Oscar Gonzalez|Dr. G]]... I hope this message finds you well. I'm closing in on my target, a big man called [[Little Rob]].|Dr. G is code for Oscar Gonzalez}} They say he lives somewhere in the mountains. In some kind of [[Deserted mine|hideout]]. You might wonder who 'they' are... I'm talking about people in the know. Squatters, prospectors, gold diggers. They say they've had run ins with the target. I met them in [[Surly's shack|a shack]] in the hills, up near [[Hemlock Holes|a golf course]] that's seen better days. But I wasn't there for the greens… We met up and made merry. Don't judge me! You're a merrymaker yourself, you know. They said they could take me to Rob. I decided to follow. Dangerous, I know, but you have to take some risks if you're gonna get the big score. That's just how it is in this business. I'll see you on the other side. Hunter out.
}}

'''Tragedy Hits Hornwright'''

Monday, August 25, 2076. [[Charleston]]. Visionary entrepreneur [[Daniel Hornwright]] lays his late wife [[Evelyn Hornwright|Evelyn]] to rest today, after her long battle with [[cancer]] finally ended early Monday morning at their peaceful summer home. Although she held no official position within the company, employees reacted with tearful silence when being informed of her passing. Sacramental Glade.wikitext:
{{Infobox incomplete|FO76OB|Location data}} {{Infobox location |games =FO76,FO76OB |type =pond lake |image =FO76OB Sacramental Glade 01.png |map marker ='''Sacramental Glade''' |map marker image =Cranberry Glade map.png |part of =[[Cranberry Bog]], [[Appalachia]] |events =[[Beasts of Burden|Event: Beasts of Burden]] |quests =[[Cop a Squatter|Daily: Cop a Squatter]] |factions =[[Cult of the Mothman]] |buildings = |founded by = |leaders =[[Adelaide|Elder Adelaide]] {{Icon|mentioned}} |owners = |creatures = |robots = |crafting = |terminal = |cell name = |edid = |formid = |refid = |keywords = }} The '''Sacramental Glade''' is a [[Fallout 76 locations|location]] in the [[Cranberry Bog]] region of [[Appalachia]] {{in|FO76}}. Previously known as [[Cranberry Glade]], it was renovated and renamed by the [[Cult of the Mothman]] at the time of the ''[[Once in a Blue Moon]]'' [[Fallout 76 updates|update]]. The public event [[Beasts of Burden]] takes place here. ==Background== {{See also|Cranberry Glade}} The Sacramental Glade is a natural cranberry glade''[[Fallout 76 Vault Dweller's Survival Guide Atlas of Appalachia]]'' CRANBERRY GLADE p. 490:
''"This natural glade of boggy ground where cranberries still grow is now lightly irradiated. Find a small gravel pit and cooking area in the parking lot, and seek out a stranded musicians' coach if you can find it in the mist."'' that served as a park before the War. It consisted of a network of wooden walkways throughout a marshy thicket. The site was settled by the Cult of the Mothman in [[Timeline (2100-2149)#2104|2104]].[[Once in a Blue Moon]] takes place in 2104. The cultists were tracking an [[Ogua]] in the area, and decided to build shelters in the glade while preparing for their hunt. They hoped to sacrifice the creature to the [[Mothman]].[[A worthy sacrifice]] The Cult began incubating mothman eggs within one of these sealed, elevated shacks for safekeeping. During this time, one of the cult members, [[Adelaide|Elder Adelaide]], met [[Luca Costa]], a [[Blue Ridge Caravan Company]] traveling merchant. The Elder posed as a trader and lured Luca Costa into an ambush. Though he escaped, the cult took possession of [[Moona Lisa|his pack animal]], his supplies, and a number of crude explosives and kept them in the glade.[[A blessed gift]]Events of [[Beasts of Burden]] ==Layout== [[File:76 OIABM Sacramental Glade mist.png|thumb]] Set in a marshy thicket and built on a pre-War network of wooden walkways, the Sacramental Glade consists of several elevated wooden shacks and outdoor ritual spaces. There is one small shack on the ground level, and a barn-like structure. ==Notable loot== * [[A blessed gift]] - Note, on the northern end of the location, along the rope bridge levels, on a small bench at a circular area covered by several canopies. * [[A worthy sacrifice]] - Note, on the western side of the location, near its entrance. It is at an elevated shrine area, near several candle shrines and a coffin, on a small bench. ==Notes== * There are small empty elevated cultist shacks which can only be entered during the event. * [[Cultist (Fallout 76)|Cultists]] spawn here during the Beasts of Burden event. They have no animation markers in the area, and will mill about when inactive. They may wade out into the mists that pool here. ** As of ''[[Expeditions: Atlantic City]]'', cultists now populate the Glade normally, regardless of whether the event has been recently activated. They still have no animation markers. * The closest cultist presences are the ritual camp at [[Old Mold Quarry]] and the bonfire due south of [[Watoga]]. * When standing on a particular section of the elevated walkways, [[Pylon V-13]] can be seen through a clearing in the trees. ==Appearances== The Sacramental Glade appears only {{In|FO76OB}}. ==Behind the scenes== Among the developers who worked on the creation of the Sacramental Glade was [[Double Eleven]] level designer [[Courtney Raine]], who also worked on [[Nuka-World on Tour (location)|Nuka-World on Tour]].[https://twitter.com/sweilous/status/1704891504995586545 Courtney Raine on Twitter]: ''"Some of the level design work I have done for @Fallout
Worked with excellent people to bring these concepts to life! #leveldesign #Fallout"'' ==Gallery== FO76OB Sacramental Glade 02.png|Entrance sign FO76OB Sacramental Glade 03.png|Outer shack FO76OB Sacramental Glade 04.png|Upper levels FO76OB Sacramental Glade 05.png|View of central complexes FO76OB Sacramental Glade 06.png|Skeletons on pews FO76OB Sacramental Glade 07.png|Repurposed airplane wing as a walkway to a shack 76 OIABM Sacramental mists.png 76 OIABM Sacramental Glade pews.png 76 OIABM Sacramental Glade overview.png FO76 Cranberry Glade cultist 01.jpg|Сultist FO76 Cranberry Glade cultists chapel.jpg|Chapel FO76 Cranberry Glade (Moon Ambush Cultist Note2).jpg|[[A blessed gift]] FO76_Cranberry_Glade_(Moon_Ambush_Cultist_Note1).jpg|[[A worthy sacrifice]] ==References== {{References}} '''Non-game''' {{References|group="Non-game"}} {{Navbox Once in a Blue Moon}} {{Navbox locations FO76}} [[Category:Fallout 76 locations]] [[Category:Once in a Blue Moon locations]] [[Category:Cranberry Bog locations]] [[ru:Священная поляна]] [[zh:聖禮林地]]

'''A blessed gift''' is a [[Fallout 76 notes|paper note]] {{in|FO76OB}}.

==Location==
The note can be found at the [[Sacramental Glade]], on the northern end of the location, along the rope bridge levels, on a small bench at a circular area covered by several canopies.

==Transcript==
{{Transcript|text=
Holy [[Mothman]], once again you have granted us such benevolent opportunities.

Whilst tracking [[Ogua|the creature]], [[Adelaide|Elder Adelaide]] stumbled upon [[Luca Costa|a mindless merchant]] traveling the roads and crafted a wise, guileful scheme. She posed as a trader and organized a deal for later that week.

We spent days crafting an ambush.
When the time came, we overpowered the fool and took his supplies, ammunition and pack animal... though the coward knew better than to fight back. 

Some explosive contraptions were also among the plunder. They appear crude but will be effective none the less. Was this another gift from you, oh divine one?
This thundering wrath could aid us in raining hellfire on our enemy.

We pray for your continued guidance. Soon, you will bear witness to a worthy offering and your merciful kindness will be rewarded.
}}

==Behind the scenes==
During the [[Public Test Server]] for ''Once in a Blue Moon'', this note's transcript was shorter and did not mention the ambush plan or Elder Adelaide, instead only saying that the merchant stumbled into their path and that they overcame him.

'''A worthy sacrifice''' is a [[Fallout 76 notes|paper note]] {{in|FO76OB}}.

==Location==
The note can be found at the [[Sacramental Glade]], on the western side of the location, near its entrance. It is at an elevated shrine area, near several candle shrines and a coffin, on a small bench.

==Transcript==
{{Transcript|text=
Oh my shepherd. Such blessings [[Mothman|you]] have cast upon us.

Grant us your strength once more, for we have found [[Ogua|a beast]] worthy of being sacrificed in your holy name. 

It's{{sic}} blood is ancient, holding secrets of long ago.

The creature has traveled south and we have trudged through the night in pursuit of the hunt, though our endeavors thus far have proved unfruitful.

The monster is strong and savage, snapping in two those that dare step near its vicious jaws.

It appears to have taken up residency near a vast bog, and we too have created shelter here whilst we prepare defenses and plans to vanquish it. 

When the time is right, blood will spill and it shall offer your divine sight visions of ages past.
}}
